The obligation `disposition` vocabulary here is PROPOSED: the authoritative dossier document is Phase 2, and if it lands a different vocabulary this schema becomes export-bundle/2 rather than being edited in place. No field in this document can hold a numeric confidence: `confidence` is a label under a pinned scheme, and additionalProperties is false everywhere
title: Canonical research export bundle
description: What every export sink receives: the topic's approved research record in one versioned shape. Assembled by code from committed state — never by an agent, and never from agent prose. It carries only material already approved for publication (the manifest that accompanies it names the approval), so a bundle is never a route by which unapproved work leaves the engine. Source content appears only where the record says it may be redistributed; everything else is referenced by locator. Nothing in a bundle is evidence that delivery happened: delivery lives in export-delivery-receipt.schema.json, and completion lives in the dossier the bundle points at.

contract.description: The approved contract revision the work was conducted under (G-1: hash-locked with its protocol revision).

assembler_version.description: The identity of the code that assembled this bundle, as dossiers carry evaluator_version. A bundle is a pure function of (approved revision, bundle_version, export options, assembler_version): the same inputs assemble byte-identically, which is what lets a sink treat redelivery as idempotent.

allOf.description: A bundle with no source content may carry no quote (content_policy is the single place that answer is recorded).

completion.description: Scientific completion, one of the three independent facts (P-4). Delivery and surveillance currency are NOT here: a bundle that cannot be delivered is still a bundle of a completed topic, and a stale feed does not rewrite this. A qualified conclusion is always conditional on framing, coverage and discovery mechanisms (G-9), so those three statements are required when that is the outcome — a completion that cannot state them is not this outcome.

residual_uncertainty.description: Required by G-9 when the topic stopped for resources: the stop is never relabeled as saturation, and the uncertainty it left is stated.

importance.description: The operator-confirmed rating, band first (G-2). The 1-9 score is an optional elicitation aid atop the band, never a probability; a bundle carries the operator's rating, never a Jev proposal.

confidence.description: How certain the record is about a disposition, in the form the record actually holds. Two shapes only. `recorded_assessment` is a LABEL from a scheme pinned by id and version, with the invocation that assessed it — the primary agent's judgment within the protocol, attributed. `unknown` states that no assessment exists and why. There is deliberately no numeric field in either shape: an LLM label never carries an invented probability (BOUNDARIES.md *Decision layer*), and additionalProperties: false makes one unrepresentable rather than discouraged. This schema does not legislate a certainty scale; the scheme the labels come from is declared by the contract revision.

obligation.description: One obligation of the approved contract with its disposition. `supported` and `not_supported` are both answers; `insufficient_evidence` means the search was adequate and nothing sufficient was found; `unknown` means coverage itself is not established (a degraded or unobserved window) and is never read as a null result (RG-U). `mixed` records a conflict and keeps it — disagreement is never averaged.

allOf.description: An unresolved or unestablished disposition says why; it never stands as a bare label.
RG-U: an unknown-coverage obligation cannot also report an assessed confidence — there is nothing assessed to be confident about.
A supported obligation cites the claims that support it.
An obligation with no accepted evidence cites none: `unknown` and `insufficient_evidence` never carry support.
A recorded conflict has an open or recorded adjudication item, not a silent average.

claim.description: A claim of the record at the revision it was exported at. Claim text is the engine's own synthesis statement, not retrieved source content; retrieved text travels only as a quote on a link, under the content policy. `provisional` is absent from the status enum on purpose: a bundle carries the record's dispositions, not its scratch capture state.

allOf.description: A load-bearing claim declares the access tier its verification had to reach (the DDL requires the same).

claim_source_link.description: One claim's link to one source, with the tier the check actually reached. Tiers are different checks, not interchangeable 'verified' flags: an abstract check never satisfies a full-text requirement (V-2). A load-bearing claim's link must name a verification receipt — a tier-0 entailment pass is a screen and never stands in for verification.

source_id.description: The gateway source the record came from (its registry id, e.g. `crossref`), so an export can be traced to a lane and its licence verdict.

locator.description: The identity the record is reachable by (a DOI, a persistent identifier, a URL). Exports carry locators, never fetched content.

supporting_quote.description: An exact quote from the source, included ONLY where the record says that source's content may be redistributed. `redistributable` is a const true, so a quote whose posture is prohibited or unknown cannot be represented at all — it is omitted, and the omission is recorded in content_policy.omitted_for_licence. The licence is the CONTENT licence the source reported for the work, which is a different question from the source's metadata terms.

allOf.description: V-1/V-2: a load-bearing link carries a verification receipt, at a named tier.

synthesis_view.description: Synthesis travels as a RENDERED VIEW of the claim graph at a revision, never as the record itself (flow §5: claim-graph first, so a reframe re-renders instead of rewriting). The artifact is content-addressed; the renderer's identity and the graph revision are what make the view reproducible.

stopping_dossier.description: The dossier the completion was ruled on, carried permanently with the bundle (design review §8: every completion permanently carries its evidence). Per-rule operands are typed counts, so an unobserved operand stays unobserved: a satisfied rule may not rest on one.

operands.description: What the rule was evaluated over: named counts that can be observed, partial or unknown.

thresholds.description: The rule's declared parameters, from the approved contract.

allOf.description: RG-U made checkable: a satisfied rule has no unknown operand.

resource_limit_reached.description: Recorded separately from every scientific rule, so a budget stop can never satisfy a completion condition (G-11).

candidate_units.description: The four units evidence accounting keeps distinct (adjudication (b)7). Each is an observed count, so an unobserved window travels as unknown with its reason and never as a zero denominator.

content_policy.description: The one place a bundle answers 'may this content leave the engine'. Redistribution is a per-record question the gateway answers per record (it records a `redistributable` flag and the content licence beside each contributing payload), not a per-source one: a CC0 metadata record can describe a copyrighted paper. Omissions are listed rather than silently dropped, so an export that is thinner than the record says why.
